scenes.say: Ever wondered what a logistic regression coefficient actually tells you about your data?

scenes.label: Log-odds
scenes.sub: Logistic regression models binary outcomes using log-odds.
scenes.say: Logistic regression predicts binary outcomes by modeling the log-odds of the event.
First, the coefficient shows how the log-odds change for each unit increase. Next, exponentiate it to get the odds ratio. That tells you how much the odds multiply.

scenes.title: Logit(p) = 1.5x
scenes.say: For example, a coefficient of one point five means the odds multiply by about four point five for each unit increase.

scenes.question: What does the coefficient mean?
scenes.wrong: It shows the change in probability.
scenes.right: It shows the change in log-odds. To get the change in odds, exponentiate the coefficient.
scenes.say: Don’t confuse the coefficient with a change in probability. It actually represents the change in log-odds. You need to exponentiate it to see the effect on odds.
